title: Introduce manifest fingerprinting and sealed-bootstrap flow with rollback guard
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Private installer deployments were occasionally failing during tenant bootstrap when parallel installs applied overlapping RBAC manifests; rollbacks could leave partially-applied roles that broke subsequent upgrades. This PR introduces a manifest fingerprinting mechanism, a sealed-bootstrap orchestration mode (no external credentials required during in-cluster seeding), and a rollback guard to detect and safely revert only fully-applied policy bundles. Scope: adds a deterministic fingerprint to each generated RBAC/policy bundle, consolidates bootstrap permissions into a single ephemeral controller role, implements a staged-apply planner that validates idempotence via plan-diff and fingerprint checks, and adds a preflight network+policy scan to the Helm preinstall hook to ensure tenant isolation constraints. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and architecture review complete - [x] End-to-end integration tests for bootstrap and rollback - [x] Terraform module backwards compatibility tests - [x] Helm chart bump and values schema update - [x] Security review for reduced-privilege bootstrap flow Implementation summary: - Manifest fingerprinting: a SHA256 of normalized YAML (sorted keys, stripped timestamps) is appended as annotations/redwood.io/manifest-fingerprint to all generated Role, RoleBinding, ClusterRole, and ClusterRoleBinding manifests. This enables deterministic detection of whether a bundle was applied unchanged. - Sealed-bootstrap mode: bootstrap-controller runs with a sealed-serviceaccount token pattern; it fetches encrypted secrets from the installer step (local disk or cloud KMS) and performs tenant-scoped seeding without long-lived elevated credentials. - Staged-apply planner: computes plan-diff against live cluster and refuses to apply if non-fingerprint changes are detected unless explicitly forced with --force-unmanaged. - Rollback guard: on upgrade failure, the operator will only revert bundles whose fingerprints match the last successful apply; bundles with divergent fingerprints are marked for manual investigation and left intact to prevent accidental privilege escalation or data loss. - Preflight policy scan: Helm preinstall hook now runs a lightweight admission-style check that verifies VPC networkPolicy templates and namespace-affinity rules to catch tenant isolation regressions before apply. Migrations and compatibility: - Terraform module change: outputs now include bundle_fingerprint and sealed_bootstrap_enabled flags. Existing installs will continue to run in legacy bootstrap mode unless the new sealed flag is set. - Helm values: added .sealedBootstrap.enabled (false default), .rbac.bundleFingerprintPolicy (hash|none), and preflight.enabled (true default for private deployments). Testing: - Unit tests for fingerprint normalization and deterministic ordering - Integration CI job added (private-installer/e2e-bootstrap) exercising sealed-bootstrap with KMS mock - Manual validation documented in docs/installer/README-sealed-bootstrap.md Rollout plan: - Canary deploy on low-load private tenants for 48h with staged-apply logs enabled - Monitor SLOs and audit logs for any unexpected role bindings - If any plan-diff mismatches occur, abort rollout and open ENG-PRIV-ISSUE for manual triage Security considerations: - Sealed-bootstrap reduces blast radius by using ephemeral controller credentials and KMS-sealed payloads - Fingerprint annotations are non-sensitive and only used for idempotence checks - Audit trail inclusion: installer records fingerprint and plan hash to the tenant audit log Files changed (high level): - installer/pkg/bootstrap/controller.go (new sealed bootstrap controller and rollback guard) - installer/templates/rbac/*.yaml (added fingerprint annotations and normalization) - helm/redwood-private/values.schema.json (new fields) - terraform/modules/private-bootstrap/outputs.tf (fingerprint outputs) - docs/installer/README-sealed-bootstrap.md (new doc) - ci/jobs/e2e-bootstrap.yaml (added integration job) Example normalized snippet used for fingerprinting (normalized YAML one-liner): "apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1;kind:Role;metadata:{name:tenant-admin,namespace:tenant-123,annotations:{'redwood.io/manifest-fingerprint':"<sha256>"}};rules:[{apiGroups:[''],resources:['pods'],verbs:['get','list']}]" Commits summary: - add: sealed-bootstrap controller and manifest fingerprinting || - feat: staged-apply planner and rollback guard || - chore: helm values schema and terraform outputs || - test: e2e private-installer job and unit tests || - docs: sealed-bootstrap usage and migration guide
Review comments: Ethan Z: Please ensure fingerprinting normalization is stable across Go YAML serializers; prefer canonical JSON pathing if possible.
Maya L: We need a clear admin recovery path documented in case preflight blocks valid customer network setups.
Ibrahim K: CI flaked on e2e with KMS mock, re-run after fix to mock logic.
Sofia P (author): Addressed serializer stability by switching to canonical JSON marshalling; added recovery steps to docs and tightened KMS mock in CI.
release_notes: Added sealed-bootstrap mode and manifest fingerprinting for safer tenant bootstrap and rollback behavior. Defaults preserve existing installs but enable improved idempotence and rollback safety when activated.
